d: Binance is a leading global blockchain ecosystem behind the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange by trading volume and registered users. We are trusted by 300+ million people in 100+ countries for our industry-leading security, user fund transparency, trading engine speed, deep liquidity, and an unmatched portfolio of digital-asset products. Binance offerings range from trading and finance to education, research, payments, institutional services, and more. Our mission is to increase the freedom of money and financial access for people around the world.

We are looking for a Policy & Change Management Specialist to strengthen governance and operational effectiveness across the Compliance function. You will drive the end-to-end policy lifecycle, change management, governance reporting and risk oversight, ensuring compliance frameworks remain accurate, consistent and audit-ready across multiple jurisdictions. You will also have the opportunity to leverage AI and automation to modernize governance processes, improve efficiency and strengthen risk oversight, partnering closely with Compliance, Legal, Product and Internal Controls teams.
q: 3–5+ years of experience in compliance policy governance, change management or regulatory program management within financial services.
Working knowledge of AML/BSA, sanctions compliance and country risk requirements.
Proven experience managing policy/document governance, change management workflows, approvals, attestations and audit-ready records.
Experience supporting regulatory examinations, audits or internal control reviews, including evidence coordination and remediation tracking.
Strong capabilities in governance reporting, stakeholder coordination, documentation and managing multiple priorities across jurisdictions.
Proficiency in Confluence, document management systems, structured trackers and dashboards.
Familiarity with AI tools for research, drafting, analysis and workflow automation, with sound judgment in handling confidential information.
Experience in the cryptocurrency, digital assets or fintech industry.
Exposure to regulatory change monitoring, country risk assessments and multi-jurisdictional compliance frameworks.
Experience implementing AI-driven workflow automation or governance process improvements.
Collaborate with world-class talent in a user-centric global organization with a flat structure
Tackle challenging projects in a fast-paced and innovative enviornment with autonomy
Thrive in a results-driven workplace with opportunities for career growth and continuous learning
Remote-first, work-from-home arrangement (may vary depending on the nature of the role and team)

r: Manage the global and local compliance policy lifecycle, including document governance, version control, periodic reviews, approvals and central repository maintenance.
Drive end-to-end policy and process change management, including impact assessments, stakeholder communications, implementation tracking and adherence to agreed timelines.
Coordinate governance processes covering attestations, exceptions, deviations and remediation actions, ensuring timely approvals, follow-ups and accurate record keeping.
Monitor the Compliance Roadmap, country risk ratings and regulatory developments, supporting risk assessments, annual recalibrations and implementation updates.
Deliver governance reporting, year-end policy assessments and audit or regulatory support, ensuring accurate documentation, evidence management and timely issue resolution.
Partner with Compliance, Legal, Product, Internal Controls and senior stakeholders to address policy and process queries and strengthen governance frameworks.
Drive AI-enabled automation and workflow enhancements to improve governance efficiency, reporting accuracy and risk oversight.

d: Lead design progress for Middle East public/civic building projects from concept through construction documents and site support, coordinating with the Middle East client and the Shanghai design team.
Participate in and develop schematic design, ensure spatial logic and design quality, and deliver implementable design outcomes.
Organize construction drawings and related late-stage deliverables, coordinate with structural, MEP, and other disciplines, and follow up on site technical issues and design changes.
Communicate and report in English with the Middle East client, keep the Shanghai team aligned, and ensure smooth milestones and collaboration.
Bachelor’s degree or above in Architecture or a related field, with 3+ years of architectural design experience.
Strong schematic design capability, with experience in late-stage drawings and on-site construction support.
Overseas public/civic building project experience preferred.
Fluent spoken English and strong communication skills; able to drive the project between the Middle East client and the Shanghai team.

As a Senior Data Engineer, you will build the pipelines and models the rest of DZ will run on. DZ operates across several verticals and markets: digital goods, ticketing, travel and trading, in Iraq, the UAE and KSA. Each has grown its own reporting and its own version of the numbers. As one of the first engineers in the new data team, you will own core parts of the data platform end to end, from ingestion off operational systems and third parties through to the modeled tables that finance, commercial and product use to make decisions, and the path that takes data science models from notebook to production. This role is about making data correct, fresh and trusted by default, so the answer stops depending on who pulled it.
q: 5 to 8 years building production software or data systems, with 3+ years in data engineering owning pipelines the business depended on.
Expert SQL and strong Python, solid dimensional modelling, and the judgment to choose the right model for the use case.
Hands-on experience with a cloud warehouse and modern orchestration and transformation tooling (for example dbt, Airflow or Dagster), plus working knowledge of Postgres and AWS.

Hands-on experience deploying and operating ML models in production alongside data scientists: feature pipelines, batch or real-time serving, model versioning, and monitoring (for example with MLflow, SageMaker or similar).
Experience with both batch and streaming ingestion, including change data capture, late and duplicate events, and schema evolution.
A correctness mindset: you reconcile numbers against the source, and you know a pipeline that runs green can still be wrong.
Communication that lands with technical and non-technical audiences, including the patience to get stakeholders to agree on what a metric means.
Analytics experience on e-commerce, payments, marketplace or fintech products, including multi-currency and multi-market reporting.
Experience with a feature store or MLOps platform, or with ML use cases such as fraud, risk or personalisation.
Experience on an early-stage data team, or consolidating fragmented reporting across business units.
Familiarity with TypeScript or Go, to work comfortably in the services that produce DZ's data.
r: Design, build and own production pipelines end to end, batch and streaming: ingestion from DZ's services (Postgres/Aurora, event streams) and third-party providers, with idempotent loads and backfills that are safe to rerun.
Model data for the warehouse and the semantic layer, turning agreed metric definitions into tested, documented models that give the same answer every time.

Treat data quality as part of the job, not a cleanup: tests, freshness SLAs, lineage and alerting that catch upstream breaks before a stakeholder does. You'll be an active participant in the team's on-call.
Partner with data science to take models from notebook to production: feature pipelines, training datasets, model deployment and serving, and monitoring for drift and data quality once they are live.
Work with product and engineering teams on event tracking and data contracts, so instrumentation is designed into services rather than bolted on, and schema changes stop silently breaking pipelines.
Handle sensitive data correctly by design: access control, masking and retention for PII (passport and telecom identifiers) across markets with different regulatory expectations.
Weigh cost against value in warehouse compute, storage and tooling, and make the tradeoffs visible.
Use AI-assisted development with judgment: review generated SQL and pipeline code like a peer PR, and check it against real data, not only whether it runs.
Mentor teammates and keep the platform legible through runbooks, ADRs and documented models, so you are not the only person who can support a critical pipeline.
x: Immediate, large-scale impact on a high-growth business
Work alongside top regional talent, with team members from Talabat, Careem, Etisalat, and more

d: HSBC Saudi Arabia provides investment banking services to the full spectrum of corporate and institutional clients in both the private and government sectors, including public companies; private companies and establishments; funds; government agencies; and family businesses and offices.
Role Purpose (overall high level summary of the role)

A senior management role playing a key central role overseeing, and executing key activities within the Risk and Control Framework in SSV. This will involve providing co-ordination, advice, independent challenge and assessment in relation to all risk governance, reporting and data quality activities undertaken by the NFR Function or the SSV Business/Risk Owners in line with NFRO model/FIM.
This will include, inter-alia, managing and delivering the following (or a subset thereof as agreed with management):

NFR Policy& Assurance – To understand and interpret all NFR requirements (and changes thereto) and to provide on-going assurance and reporting regarding global adherence with requirements, working closely with MENA NFR teams and 2LOD stakeholders;
FIM Policy – To understand the FIM Policy Framework and to manage and oversee the cascade and adoption of any changes thereto;
Governance & Reporting – To oversee, support and deliver fit for purpose risk governance arrangements and related reporting (and other ad-hoc reporting as required);

Assurance & Monitoring – To assist the NFR function in the consistent design and delivery a suitable risk based assurance and monitoring programme (including substantive control testing (ICMP), KRI and Thematic Reviews (supporting the SSV Non-Financial Risk Analysis Team))
Risk & Control Assessment (RCA) – To assist the NFR function to ensure the SSV RCA is dynamically maintained, based on all relevant risk triggers;

Supporting as required any related risk and control related activities including, but not restricted to, liaison with Internal/External Audit and Regulatory Authorities as well as key internal stakeholder.
r: Key activities and decision making areas
Act as a senior manager within the HBSA SSV NFR function, assisting in driving management, coordination and execution of risk management activities across SSV.
Maintaining relationships with 2nd/ 3rd line of defense risk functions.
Maintain regular interaction with appropriate MSS and OPS Risk internal colleagues
Oversee the effective monitoring of risks, services and processes against agreed group/divisional standards and external requirements.
Ensure the risk governance framework is clear, fit for purpose and executed as defined, and that escalation paths are adequate and effective.
Support line management as a key point of contact for SSV risk and control framework, policies, governance and reporting arrangements.
Support the NFR and SSV Senior Management in ensuring the appropriate risk and control structure is in place and that risks that have been highlighted are managed appropriately.
Play a key role in communication across SSV, MSS, OPS Risk, Global Functions and DBS regarding the Risk and Control Agenda.
Provide consistent internal and external benchmarking, where appropriate.
Support achievement of the HBSA vision, values, goals and culture in personal behaviour, actions and decision making.

Provide technical leadership and support technical excellence by searching out external best practice, monitoring technical and professional developments, sharing knowledge and encouraging others to do the same in the best interests of HSBC SA and its customers.

Encourage and enable constructive cross-country and cross-business teamwork by demonstrating collaboration and matrix management in action and challenging actions and behaviours that are not consistent with HSBC SA Standards and/or the best interests of the business and its customers.
Ensure detailed understanding, communication and execution of a robust SSV risk management framework.
Support line management and the NFR Leadership Team in driving the risk agenda across SSV, ensuring maximum awareness, management of issues and overall compliance with framework requirements
Attend as required Risk & Control related committees/forums and ensure that the agenda effectively covers critical SSV risks and issues.
Regularly review the business risk management policies and operating processes and activities.

Assist the NFR function to minimize the likelihood and impact of disruption by ensuring that the business can continue to meet at least the minimum expectations of customers, counterparties, regulators and other stakeholders at all times.
Implement oversight and assurance of the risk and control framework to ensure that operational (and other) risks are managed closely and effectively, in a commercially sensitive and practical manner.

Drive to ensure that the business inherent risk profile and any related issues/impacts are understood by the business and the appropriate actions (and/or risk acceptance) have been put in place to manage residual risk within appetite.
Major Challenges (The challenges inherent in the role that require a continual test of the role holder’s abilities)
Overseeing and assuring a diverse and complex risk, control and regulatory environment, that is continually developing/changing in scope and focus.
Keeping up to date regarding external developments in global regulation, market trends and competitor activity.
Working as part of a truly global business operating in 38 countries, meeting Group standards of risk management, while understanding the commercial realities of SSV’ institutional client base.
Working with internal and external stakeholders to shape a sustainable future for SSV.
To respectfully challenge the risk profile with peers across MSS and relevant Global Functions, maintaining a balance between risk reward/commercial benefit.
Role Context (The environment and operating conditions of the role including the extent of guidance and authority)
Primary functional and entity reporting relationship to the Head of SSV, NFR Governance, Reporting and Data Analysis
Close working relationship with the relevant NFR teams at all levels.
Close working relationships with relevant stakeholders and peers across MSS, and Group Functions (Risk & Control related)
Key role in the SSV Risk Governance and Reporting processes and all related NFR related activities.
To deputize management at SSV and MSS Governance Forums as requested.
Observation of Internal Controls (Compliance Policy / FIM requirements)

The jobholder will also adhere to, and be able to demonstrate adherence to, internal controls. This will be achieved by adherence to all relevant procedures, keeping appropriate records and, where appropriate, by the timely implementation of internal and external audit points, including issues raised by external regulators.

The jobholder will implement the HBSA Compliance Policies by containing compliance risk in liaison with the HBSA Heads of Compliance (Regulatory and Financial Crime). The term ‘compliance’ embraces all relevant financial services laws, rules and codes with which the business has to comply. This will be achieved by adhering to all relevant processes/procedures and by liaising with Compliance department about new business initiatives at the earliest opportunity.

Also, and when applicable, this will be achieved by ensuring adequate resources are in place to deliver to compliance requirements, ensuring training is provided and by fostering a compliance culture.
Knowledge & Experience / Qualifications (For the role – not the role holder. Minimum requirements of the role.)
Educated to undergraduate or post-graduate degree level in Accountancy, Finance or related field.
Strong leadership and management ability, including motivating employees in the wider organisation.
Deep understanding of HSBC structures, processes and objectives, especially in the risk environment.
Broad knowledge of the external environment (regulatory, political, competitors etc.).
Deep knowledge of HSBC and MSS: functionally, operationally and financially.
High level of drive and motivation to ensure delivery of a broad range of outputs simultaneously.
Proven ability to articulate complex issues concisely and in clear language.
Use judgement and experience to determine how to handle complex requests and varying timescales; make judgements quickly and consistently.
Relationship management and collaboration skills: ability to form effective relationships and achieve influence with peers across the organisation.
Interpersonal skills: proven ability to communicate effectively and confidently at all levels across the Group.
Practical experience of major business tranformation activities.
Proven abilities in managing virtual teams and working across cultures in a global business context.
